Please review the following manuscript you wrote before.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-r4q77lpb/call-aba9f7ac8b994b15b55500f5758c2d74/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la . manuscript.pdf; command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for module in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(module)
    print(module, spec.origin if spec else 'unavailable')
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs
python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
    text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') for i,p in enumerate(r.pages)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem with a straightforward pipeline combining representative feature targets and class-specific BatchNorm matching, avoiding differentiation through student training.

Reported results are promising across three datasets and multiple compression budgets. At 50 images per class, WMDD achieves 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet versus CDA’s 48.7%, and 57.6% on ImageNet-1K versus 53.5%. Repeated runs and error bars strengthen the empirical reporting.

The experiments include useful component ablations, regularization sensitivity, qualitative comparisons, and transfer across architectures. Table 2 demonstrates particularly useful transfer within the ResNet family.

The manuscript attributes the underlying optimal-transport solver, synthesis framework, and datasets. The appendices provide training hyperparameters and acknowledge pretrained-model dependence, computational overhead, and inherited dataset bias.
weaknesses: The novelty of the central formulation needs clarification. With squared Euclidean cost and freely optimized support weights, Eq. (7) reduces to ordinary k-means quantization: minimizing the average squared distance to the nearest support point. The single-distribution constrained-barycenter interpretation is mathematically possible, but the missing connection to quantization and absence of a k-means-feature-inversion baseline leave the claimed contribution insufficiently distinguished.

The optimized probability measure is not clearly connected to the dataset actually used for training. Algorithm 2 learns nonuniform weights, but Eq. (16), Algorithm 1’s output, and the student-training description do not explain how these weights are retained. Without corresponding weighted sampling or training, matching support locations does not reproduce the optimized distribution.

The ablations provide limited support for attributing improvements specifically to Wasserstein matching. In Table 3, cross-entropy plus class-specific BatchNorm already achieves 64.0/41.3/37.4%, compared with 64.8/41.8/38.2% for the complete method. Table 4 does not establish that feature extractors and regularization are matched between methods. Moreover, at one image per class, the stated squared-Wasserstein objective targets the feature mean, weakening the proposed geometric explanation for its advantage over mean matching.

Baseline comparability is unresolved. SRe2L achieves 21.3% on ImageNet-1K at 10 images per class in Table 1, whereas the stated baseline in Table 3 achieves 36.1%. Against WMDD’s 38.2%, this changes the apparent improvement from 16.9 to 2.1 percentage points. The discrepancy and any differences in teacher, relabeling, augmentation, or student training require reconciliation.

The optimization explanation contains consequential ambiguities. The quadratic Hessian argument in Section 4.2.2 applies with the transport plan fixed; it does not establish convexity of the minimized transport objective over support locations. Algorithm 2 updates weights but reuses the preceding transport plan, and zero weights can make the position update undefined. The PDF also leaves barycenter initialization, iteration count, and learning-rate settings unspecified.

The efficiency evidence does not adequately support the ImageNet-scale overhead claim. Appendix F measures only ImageNette at one image per class, where the optimal support is simply a centroid. Measurements at larger support budgets, with transport computation and the other pipeline stages accounted for, are needed to establish practical scaling.
